absent: Backing page order selection beyond single page allocation and node placement policy
Size class table sizing, count selection, and occupancy band thresholds
Handle cache lifetime, handle allocation failure handling, and handle reuse protocol
Full zspage and descriptor structure layouts beyond fields observed here
Free chain tag bit widths and huge page object access path
Zone statistic threshold tuning and global counter aggregation
Swap cluster acquisition internals and swap cache deletion details
Working set shadow creation and file cache removal helpers
Control group hierarchy walk limits and event delivery mechanics
Generation based reclaim enablement and sequence wrap handling

findings.text: Pool lookup maps a caller request plus handle overhead to a size class entry, with index selection increasing stepwise from a floor size and saturating at the final class.

Handle and zspage metadata allocations clear high memory and movability request bits before drawing from their dedicated caches, keeping control structures in directly accessible and unmovable memory.

A zspage owns an ordered chain of descriptors linked through a next field with each descriptor pointing back to its parent, the head cached in the parent and flagged as first, and a huge marker set when the configuration holds a lone object in a lone page.
Fresh zspage records carry a magic tag plus owning pool and class identity with a newly initialized guard in unlocked state before any backing pages are attached.
Each zspage guard combines a lock dependency map with a spin guard and an explicit unlocked counter value established at creation.

Backing pages for compressed storage are allocated singly per node, marked as belonging to this allocator, counted in the dedicated zone statistic, and returned to the buddy system on release with the mark treated as sticky until handoff.

Initialization walks the chained pages and links every object slot into a single free chain with tagged links and a distinct terminator at the tail, leaving the head positioned at the start of the chain.

The offset of the first object within each backing page is stored in a masked field that only accepts values within a bounded page size ceiling and is only valid on pages already marked for this allocator.
Allocation prefers the fullest non empty fullness band, scanning occupancy bands from high to low and returning the first available zspage encountered.

Object placement consumes the current free head, advances the head from the stored link tag, records the caller handle with an allocated mark in the slot header or in the head descriptor for huge pages, updates occupancy, and publishes the encoded location through the handle.
An object reference packs the backing page frame number together with class identity and object index into separate bit fields of a single word.
Marking a zspage movable visits each descriptor in chain order and sets the movable operations flag only while holding that descriptor exclusive guard, warning if the guard cannot be acquired.

Zone counters use per processor difference buffers with a threshold that spills to the global count with hysteresis, protected against preemption, with one path for callers already safe against interrupts and another that preserves interrupt state around the update.
The swap writeout helper for the scanned context reports success without performing input output.

Mapping removal holds the swap cluster guard with interrupts disabled for swap cache entries, and the host guard plus the page tree guard with interrupts disabled for file entries, across the busy and dirty checks until the entry is detached or the attempt is abandoned.
Busy detection freezes the expected reference count before testing dirtiness with ordering that prevents a concurrent get plus dirty plus put sequence from losing newly dirtied data.

Removal requires a locked folio whose mapping matches the target, rejects unfreezable or dirty folios, and optionally installs a working set shadow only for reclaimed entries when the address space remains live, with file entries further limited to file least recently used and non direct access mappings.
Successful file detachment releases the tree and host guards, queues shrinkable inodes for later reclaim, and invokes the address space release hook when present.
Write failure handling serializes on the folio guard and records the error in the mapping only if the folio still belongs to that mapping at lock time.

Legacy swapout accounting charges the closest online ancestor for swap, records its identity across the swapped range, clears the folio control association, and adjusts memory and combined memory swap counters to reflect the move from memory to swap.

Swapout accounting expects the swap cluster guard held with interrupts disabled and updates per processor statistics under a nested preemption guard with an explicit check that interrupts remain disabled.

Control group page events distinguish inbound from outbound movement for event counts while accumulating volume in per processor counters, and threshold plus soft limit work is gated by per target rate limits driven from those counters.
Threshold notification keeps an ordered array with a cursor for the highest crossed entry, signaling crossings in either direction when usage moves and then repositioning the cursor to the new band.
Usage for the root control group is approximated from global file and anonymous states plus consumed swap when swap is queried, while other groups read their dedicated memory or combined counters.

Least recently used generation rotation for control groups assigns a random bin, moves the list node between generation queues according to head tail old or young operations, maintains per generation counts, and advances the global sequence once the oldest generation drains.
Generation rotation for control groups serializes on the per node control list guard with interrupt state preserved across segment and generation updates plus list splicing and counter maintenance.

Soft limit maintenance either delegates to generation based reclaim when that mode is active or refreshes the per node excess tree for the group and all ancestors when excess exists or the node remains queued.
Reclaim vector lookup returns the per node vector of the given control group after ensuring its node back pointer is set, falling back to the node global vector when no group is supplied.
Zspage creation unwinds partial progress on backing page exhaustion by releasing already counted pages and the parent record before reporting failure, leaving no half linked chain visible.
Control group generation selection derives the active generation from the global sequence modulo the configured generation count.
Zspage creation strips movability from allocation requests when compaction support is unavailable, keeping backing pages unmovable.
Handle publication performs a single ordered store of the encoded object into caller visible memory.
